title: Buddy Johnson, Yank Johnson and Harrison Bones
summary: Great trombonists Buddy Johnson and Harrison Bones, who came from downriver, switched from trumpet, and had a stroke.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Well, I guess you might have known, uh, probably you might have known, uh, Buddy Johnson and Yang Johnson? No, that was before my time.
That's before your time. I didn't move to Algiers until 1949.
Yeah, that was great, that was great, that was great tramb- that was great trambow players, too. Mm-hmm. Well, you never know at Harrison Bones, either. Yeah, I knew Harrison Bones.

Well, Harrison- Harrison Bones first influenced with the trumpet. He came from down the low course road there, and they came up to him, and he came to Algiers. He came here playing the trumpet. Then from the trumpet, then he took up trombone. He took up trombone.
He got to play on the trombone. Because him and Buddy Johnson used to play together in the Excelsior Brass Band.
Yeah, he wasn't far from here, he was right over on Nunes, that's now but a couple of blocks,

huh? Who, that Harrison Bones? Harrison, yeah, he was on Nunes. Yeah, he lived right over there on Nunes Street. Yeah. Yeah. That's where he lived. So you knew- Of course, after Harrison was taking but that stroke while he was finished, he was taking but a stroke. And I got pal eyes like him. He played the same way with Tats.
